# Benchmarks

How fast is doppler, and is it getting faster? These are single-machine numbers measured by hand for each release, not in CI. Each release is measured in two builds: **portable** is the PyPI wheel, and **native** is built from source for this CPU ([builds](#builds)). The trend under each number covers every release measured on this machine.

**v0.71.0** — measured 2026-10-14 on **AMD Ryzen AI 9 465 w/ Radeon 880M**, doppler `471dc1fad`, cc (GCC) 16.2.1 20260810, 7.2.9-2-cachyos; fastest core class only (cpus 0-3,10-13).

## Notes and definitions

### Headline kernels

1. <span id="d1"></span>**FFT, complex float, 4,096 points.** One forward transform of 4,096 complex float samples (cf32), out of place. The row records its time per output bin; the headline reads the whole transform. `fft::execute_cf32[n=4096]`
2. <span id="d2"></span>**Power spectrum, 1,024 bins (Welch).** Welch power-spectral-density accumulation (window, 1,024-point FFT, magnitude squared, average) over a 65,536-sample block; throughput counts input samples. `psd::accumulate[nfft=1024]`
3. <span id="d3"></span>**FIR filter, 15 real taps.** A 15-tap real-coefficient FIR filter over complex input, 65,536 samples per round; throughput counts input samples. `fir::execute[taps=15,real]`
4. <span id="d4"></span>**Down-converter, decimate by 2.** Digital down-converter: mix to baseband, filter and decimate by 2; throughput counts input samples. `ddc::execute[rate=0.50]`
5. <span id="d5"></span>**Arbitrary resampler, ratio 1.0001.** Polyphase resampler at a ratio of 1.0001, fed in blocks of 20,480 samples; throughput counts input samples. `resamp::execute[rate=1.0001,block=20480]`
6. <span id="d6"></span>**Costas carrier loop.** A Costas loop tracking a BPSK carrier: phase detector, loop filter and NCO, per input sample. `costas::steps`
7. <span id="d7"></span>**Delay-locked loop (code tracking).** An early-prompt-late delay-locked loop tracking a spreading code, per input sample. `dll::steps`
8. <span id="d8"></span>**Symbol timing recovery.** A Gardner-style symbol synchronizer with an interpolating resampler, per input sample. `symsync::steps`
9. <span id="d9"></span>**M-PSK receiver, 4 samples per symbol.** The full M-PSK receive chain (timing, carrier, decisions) at 4 samples per symbol with the AGC off, per input sample. `mpsk_receiver::steps[sps=4,agc=0]`
10. <span id="d10"></span>**DSSS acquisition, 256-chip code.** A full code-phase by Doppler search for a 256-chip spreading code; throughput counts searched input samples. `acq::native_nc256`
11. <span id="d11"></span>**Reed-Solomon decode, 8 errors.** CCSDS Reed-Solomon (255,223) decode of one codeword carrying 8 symbol errors. `rs::decode[e=8]`
12. <span id="d12"></span>**int16 to float, from Python.** Converting a 65,536-sample int16 I/Q block to float through the Python binding, so the wheel's call overhead is included. `i16_to_f32::test_bench_steps_64k`

### Terms

<span id="builds"></span>**Builds.** *portable* is the shipped wheel; *native* is `-DDOPPLER_NATIVE=ON` (`-march=native`), built from source for this CPU. The two are measured interleaved, alternating runs, keeping each benchmark's best.

<span id="from-src"></span>**From src.** How much faster the native build is than the wheel on the same benchmark: portable time ÷ native time − 1. Kernels that vectorize gain the most; call-overhead-bound rows sit near 0%.

<span id="since-last"></span>**Since last.** Portable speed against the previous release that measured the row. Changes under 3% are grey: repeat runs of an unchanged tree move about that much.

<span id="trend"></span>**Trend.** One point per release, portable build, drawn as speed (higher is faster). A gap is a release that did not measure the row. A dashed line marks a release where the row's round changed size, so its per-unit value changed meaning there; the line breaks rather than draw a jump that is not real.

<span id="units"></span>**Units.** A C row times a round of *N* units and reports time per unit: a call, a sample, a bin, a frame, a codeword. Rows whose unit is a sample read as throughput. A row from before the snapshots recorded units (v0.43.0 to v0.72.0), with no label to supply one, reads *per iter*: the round divided by its iteration count.

<span id="row-ids"></span>**Row IDs.** The small monospace line under each name is the benchmark's own ID: what `make bench BENCH_ARGS="--c-only <component>"` (C) or `make bench-python` (Python) reports it as.
